name: Arbitrary Enlargement of One Nonconstant Row
statement: Let nonempty ample $H\subseteq Q_{F\cup\{z\}}$ have sections $B_0,B_1$ and contraction $C$, and let ample $D\supseteq C$. The four-row family $V(H,D)=(B_0\times\{00\})\cup(D\times\{01\})\cup(C\times\{10\})\cup(B_1\times\{11\})$ is ample and has first-coordinate reduction $H$. It peels to its $D$-row exactly when $H$ peels, and it is dismantlable ample exactly when both $H$ and $D$ are. If $H$ has full support, then $V(H,D)$ is a pc-minimal obstruction exactly when $H$ is a pc-minimal obstruction and $D$ is dismantlable ample. Marked oriented rows uniquely recover $H$ and $D$; no relative peeling $D\searrow C$ is required.
proof: Shadow counting separates supports into those using neither, one, or both new coordinates and proves ampleness. Lift a peeling of $H$ while retaining $D$: when an old corner has its layer mate, delete its constant lift; otherwise delete its $10$ lift and then its constant lift. Reduction of any relative chain recovers a peeling of $H$, yielding the exact positivity criterion. For forbidden $H$, old-coordinate minors commute with the construction, and each new-coordinate image is a peripheral expansion of positive sections, contraction, or $D$. Conversely a forbidden output has positive $D$ face and negative reduction $H$; inherited-overlap descent makes $H$ forbidden.
